events.title: The Great Persecution begins
events.shortBlurb: At Nicomedia the edicts of Diocletian opened the last and fiercest persecution of the early Church…
body: On 23 February 303, the feast of the Terminalia, soldiers of the Emperor Diocletian demolished the great church of Nicomedia, his eastern capital, and burned its Scriptures; the next day the first of his edicts against the Christians was published. It ordered the churches razed, the sacred books surrendered, and Christians stripped of rank, office, and civil rights, the opening of the last and severest persecution of the Roman Church.

Three further edicts followed: the clergy were imprisoned, then offered freedom at the price of sacrifice, and in 304 all the empire's inhabitants were commanded to sacrifice to the gods on pain of death. The storm fell heaviest in the East under Diocletian and his Caesar Galerius, while in Gaul and Britain, where Constantius ruled, only the first edict was enforced.

The persecution slackened after Diocletian's abdication in 305, and the dying Galerius granted toleration by his edict of 311, though Maximinus renewed it in the East until his defeat by Licinius. Peace came at last in 313 with the Edict of Milan, and the memory of its countless martyrs the Church has never forgotten.

sources.text: Eusebius, Church History (Book VIII; public-domain translation)
